# Job Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 418v–419r

---

**8:1** And-answered Bildad the-Shuchite and-said:

**8:2** "How-long [ad anah] will-you-speak [temallel] these [things],
and-[be like] a-mighty wind [ruach kabbiyr] the-words [imrei] of-your-mouth [pikha]?

**8:3** Does God [el] pervert [ye'avvet] justice [mishpat]?
Or does-Shaddai [the Almighty] pervert [ye'avvet] righteousness [tsedeq]?

**8:4** If your-sons [baneykha] sinned [chat'u] against-him,
he-sent-them-away [vayshallechem] by-the-hand of-their-transgression [be-yad pish'am].

**8:5** If you [attah] would-seek [teshacher] God [el],
and-to Shaddai you-would-plead [titchannan],

**8:6** if pure [zakh] and-upright [yashar] you [are],
surely now he-will-rouse-himself [ya'ir] over-you,
and-will-restore [ve-shillem] the-habitation [nevat] of-your-righteousness [tsidqekha].

**8:7** And-your-beginning [re'shitekha] will-be small [mits'ar],
and-your-end [acharitekha] will-be-very-great [yisgeh me'od].

**8:8** For ask [she'al] now of-the-former-generation [le-dor rishon],
and-prepare [ve-khonen] for-the-search of-their-fathers [la-cheqer avotam].

**8:9** For of-yesterday [temol] we [are] and-we-know-not [ve-lo neda],
for a-shadow [tsel] [are] our-days upon the-earth [alei arets].

**8:10** Will-they-not teach-you [yorukha], tell-you [yomeru lakh],
and-from-their-heart [mi-libbam] bring-forth [yotsi'u] words [millim]?

**8:11** Does-the-papyrus [gome] grow [yig'eh] without [be-lo] marsh [bitstsah]?
Does-the-reed [achu] grow [yisgeh] without [beli] water [mayim]?

**8:12** While-still in-its-freshness [be-ibbo], not plucked [lo yiqqatef],
before all grass [chatsir] it-withers [yivash].

**8:13** So [are] the-paths [orchot] of-all who-forget God [el];
and-the-hope [tiqvat] of-the-godless [chanef] perishes [toved].

**8:14** Whose confidence [kislo] is-cut-off [yaqot],
and-a-spider's-web [beit akavissh] [is] his-trust [mivtacho].

**8:15** He-leans [yishsha'en] upon his-house [beito] and-it-does-not stand [ve-lo ya'amod];
he-grasps-it [yachaziq] and-it-does-not hold [ve-lo yaqum].

**8:16** He [is] full-of-sap [ratov] before [lifnei] the-sun [shemesh],
and-over his-garden [gannato] his-shoots [yonaqto] go-out [tetse].

**8:17** Over a-heap [gal] his-roots [shorashav] are-entwined [yesubbu],
a-house of-stones [beit avanim] he-sees [yechezeh].

**8:18** If he-is-swallowed-up [yeballennnu] from-his-place [mi-meqomo],
and-it-denies-him [ve-kichesh bo] — 'I-have-not seen-you [lo re'itikha].'

**8:19** Behold, that [is] the-joy [mesos] of-his-way [darkho],
and-from the-dust [me-afar] others [acher] will-spring-up [yitsmach].

**8:20** Behold, God [el] will-not reject [lo yim'as] the-blameless [tam],
and-he-will-not grasp [lo yachaziq] the-hand [be-yad] of-evildoers [mere'im].

**8:21** He-will-yet fill [ye-malle] your-mouth [pikha] with-laughter [sechoq],
and-your-lips [usfateykha] with-a-shout-of-joy [teruah].

**8:22** Your-haters [sone'eykha] will-be-clothed [yilbeshu] with-shame [boshet],
and-the-tent [ohel] of-the-wicked [resha'im] will-be-no-more [einennu]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "he sent them away by the hand of their transgression":** Bildad's most brutal line — he suggests Iyyov's children died because of their own sin. The Hebrew *vayshallechem be-yad pish'am* implies God dispatched them through their own offense. This is theological cruelty disguised as logic.

**v.11-12 — The papyrus metaphor:** The image is drawn from Egyptian marshland — papyrus (*gome*, the same word used for Moshe's basket) requires standing water. Cut off from its source, it withers before any other plant. Bildad applies this to the godless: without God, they cannot sustain themselves.

**v.14 — "spider's web":** The trust of the godless is compared to a *beit akavissh* (literally "house of a spider") — a structure that appears functional but collapses at the slightest pressure.

---
*— EMET*
